items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: I think Chubby Jackson was the first one to start playing that five string

ctx.x: Well, what did he -- I mean, just apart from playing the bass in there, what did he contribute to the

He contributed that -- I don't know what note it is on the bass but when the band would be swinging and nothing but the rhythm section would be -- you know, the whole band would lay out and they would call it the strolling bass, the walking bass, you know. He would go way up, (Humming) and come right on down. And he started that. And he started with four strings. And the bass players, after they started hearing it, they couldn't get that high on the bass so they started making a five string bass with that extra…

Because he went way beyond the keyboard of the bass, whatever that is. He'd go almost down to the sound post, you know, bing, bing, bing (humming). You know. Oh, man. And when the band would start doing that, oh, man. It used to send chills up me every night when I'd hear the rhythm section. The whole band would be shouting, you know. And we'd get to like the middle part, the bridge, and all of a sudden it would just -- everybody would drop out but the rhythm section (humming). Oh, my goodness.
